content.comment_body: Hello, Does anyone know if it's possible to upgrade from [version_no] to [version_no] on an Apple Macbook? On my work computer using Windows 7, I was able to complete the upgrade using the Update Center in [product_name]. On my home Apple Macbook Pro, I encounter an error (see attachment). I haven't performed upgrades on the Mac, only did a first installation using a CD I bought with [product_name] [article_no] (as an ISO file, since my Mac doesn't have a CD drive). Hoping someone can assist.
You can download an upgrade installer from the [company_name] website that offers demo software, updates, and drivers. After downloading, run the installer as administrator.

Thanks for the information! Unfortunately, when running the downloaded file "Setup.app", I get an error stating the file is damaged and needs to be sent to the trash. No other options seem possible. Using macOS Sierra 10.12.4 on Macbook Pro mid 2014. Are other Mac users experiencing this issue?

Don't use Safari browser to download the file, as it may get damaged during automatic extraction. Try expanding setup.zip with Stuffit Expander – but use version 14 or 15 only, since version 16 did not work in my experience.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having problems updating [product_name] from [version_no] to [version_no] on MacOS, as downloaded update files often end up corrupted—particularly when downloaded with certain browsers. The update process is less clear on MacOS compared to Windows, and extraction of update files sometimes depends on third-party tools and specific versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a simple and reliable procedure for updating [product_name] on MacOS, similar to the straightforward experience on Windows.
